title: Buying Property Safely: Documents, Ownership and Wills
summary: What to check before you buy land or a house. Also, how ownership, inheritance and wills work.

body.text: Land and houses cost the most money for most families. Check a little before you pay. This saves years of fighting later.
Papers to check before you buy

items: Mother deed and the chain of title. These show how the property changed hands over the years.
The latest encumbrance certificate (EC) from the sub-registrar office. It shows loans or claims on the property.
Patta / khata and property tax receipts in the seller's name.
The approved plan and layout approval. Also check if the land is farm land or house land.
If you buy from a builder, check the project approvals and RERA registration.

body.text: How to buy, step by step

items: Check who the seller is. Also check that all legal heirs agree.
Ask a lawyer to do a title search for at least 30 years.
Sign a written agreement. Pay by bank transfer. Keep the receipts.
Register the sale deed at the sub-registrar office. Pay the stamp duty (a government tax on the sale).
Change the mutation (land records) and property tax records to your name.
In Tamil Nadu, stamp duty is about 7% of the property value and the registration fee about 4% (check the current rates).

body.text: Never pay a big advance just because you saw a photocopy. Never pay on a power of attorney (a paper that lets one person act for another) you have not checked. An agreement that is not registered may not be accepted in court.

items: If a person dies without a will (intestate), the property goes to the legal heirs under their personal law.
A will lets a person decide who gets what. It must be signed and seen by witnesses.
Sometimes you need a probate or succession certificate to move some assets to the heirs' names.
A nomination (a name added to claim the money) in a bank account or insurance policy is not the same as inheritance.

body.text: For immovable property (land and buildings) above a value set by law, you must register the sale deed. A deed that is not registered may not be accepted as proof of ownership.
Keep every original paper in a safe place. Keep certified copies in a different place.
Stamp duty and registration fee (Tamil Nadu)

items: In Tamil Nadu, stamp duty is about 7% of the property value.
The registration fee is about 4% of the property value.
These rates change. Always check the current rates.
A sale deed for immovable property must be registered under the Registration Act, 1908.
An unregistered deed may not be accepted as proof of ownership.

body.text: Title check: the papers that matter

items: Check the mother deed and the chain of title.
Get an encumbrance certificate (EC) from the sub-registrar.
Patta / chitta and property tax receipts should be in the seller's name.
Update the mutation records after purchase.
For a builder project, check the RERA registration (Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016).
Also check the approved plan.
The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 applies in many cases.
The Indian Succession Act, 1925 deals with wills.
A will must be signed by the testator and attested by 2 witnesses.

body.text: Sales through a power of attorney

items: A sale through an unregistered power of attorney may not transfer valid title.
Buying agricultural land can have state-specific restrictions.

practicalSteps: Get an encumbrance certificate and a title search before you pay.
Check that the property details and measurements in the papers match the real site.
Pay through the bank. Always ask for written receipts.
Register the deed. Collect the original paper after registration.
exceptions: For farm land, each state has its own rules on who can buy it.
Inheritance rules are different for different religions, under their personal law.

faqs.q: Is it safe to buy through a power of attorney?
faqs.a: It is risky. Courts have said a sale through an unregistered power of attorney may not give you valid ownership. Ask for a registered deed.
It depends on the asset, the will and the state. For high-value or disputed property, probate is often needed.

sources.label: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - India Code

misconceptions.myth: A notarised agreement is enough to own property.
misconceptions.fact: For land and buildings, you usually need a registered sale deed. Notarisation alone does not give you ownership.
